--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.harmonic_function()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Predict missing node labels with the harmonic function (label propagation). twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.harmonic_function()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Predict missing node labels with the harmonic function (label propagation). title: >- [Graph.harmonic_function()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Predict missing node labels with the harmonic function (label propagation). page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Predict missing node labels with the harmonic function (label propagation). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L48238-L48394){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.harmonic_function( label_name, max_iter=30, weighted=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Harmonic function](../assets/graphs/harmonic-function.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two dense four-node groups, A, B, C, D and E, F, G, H, joined by the edge D to E. Only A is labeled red and H blue, shown as badges. Each unlabeled node takes the average of its neighbors' class scores, so A's group is predicted red (accent color) and H's group blue (teal), as the card lists." width="100%"} Given a few labeled nodes (stored in the node attribute `label_name`), semi-supervised node classification guesses the labels of all the others from the network: nodes that are well connected to nodes of one class probably belong to it too. The harmonic function method (Zhu, Ghahramani and Lafferty, 2003) makes each unlabeled node's class scores the average of its neighbors' scores, with the labeled nodes held fixed, which is the same as asking where a random walk from the node is most likely to first hit a labeled node. Uses include inferring the function of unannotated genes, the topic of uncited papers, or the political leaning of accounts from a small labeled sample. The graph must be undirected. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [label_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Node attribute holding the known labels; nodes without it (or with `None`) are unlabeled. Any hashable values can be labels. This can't be the `label` column of node names, as every node has a name and so every node would count as labeled. [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[30]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of propagation steps (default 30). [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to propagate along edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph's `weighted` flag. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The predicted label of every node (labeled nodes keep theirs), keyed by node ID. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed or no node is labeled. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} With the row-normalized adjacency $P = D^{-1} A$ (labeled rows set to zero) and $B$ the one-hot matrix of known labels, $F \leftarrow P F + B$ is iterated `max_iter` times from $F = 0$, and each node takes the class with the largest score. This is NetworkX's `harmonic_function` exactly; nodes whose top scores tie exactly (for example, nodes equally far from two labels) go to the class seen first in node ID order, where NetworkX's choice depends on rounding. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~local_and_global_consistency`) : Spread known labels, letting them be overruled. [](`~cmty_label_propagation`) : Spread labels with none known in advance. [](`~personalized_pagerank`) : Score nodes by a walk that keeps returning to the seeds. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two triangles joined by a single edge, with one node of each labeled in the `group` attribute. Each label spreads over its own triangle: ::: {#c0a2bb3f .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph.from_edges([ ("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D"), ]) graph.set_node_attrs("group", {"A": "red", "F": "blue"}) predicted = graph.harmonic_function(label_name="group") {graph.get_label_from_id(n): group for n, group in predicted.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'A': 'red', 'B': 'red', 'C': 'red', 'D': 'blue', 'E': 'blue', 'F': 'blue'} ``` ::: ::: ### Guessing the karate club's factions Zachary's karate club split in two after a dispute between its instructor (member 0) and its administrator (member 33), and the `faction` attribute records which side each member joined. Giving the faction of just two members, one on each side, and counting the members whose predicted faction is wrong: ::: {#5628341b .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl karate = ec.karate_club().layout_kamada_kawai() rows = [] for first, second in [("0", "33"), ("1", "32"), ("16", "26")]: karate.set_node_attrs("known", None) karate.set_node_attrs("known", {first: 1, second: 2}) guess = karate.harmonic_function(label_name="known") karate.set_node_attrs("guess", guess) members = karate.get_node_df() wrong = members.filter(pl.col("guess") != pl.col("faction")).height rows.append({"known": f"{first} and {second}", "wrong": wrong}) pl.DataFrame(rows) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: From the two leaders, or from members 1 and 32, every member is placed right. From members 16 and 26, six of the instructor's friends are placed on the administrator's side. Member 16 can be reached only through members 5 and 6, so a walk from most of the instructor's friends is more likely to reach member 26 first. The labeled members are drawn larger: ::: {layout-ncol="2"} ::: {#81c4bf2a .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} karate.set_node_attrs("known", None) karate.set_node_attrs("known", {"0": 1, "33": 2}) guess = karate.harmonic_function(label_name="known") karate.set_node_attrs("from_leaders", guess) karate.set_node_attrs("size", 1) karate.set_node_attrs("size", 2, nodes=["0", "33"]) karate.plot( layout="pos", color_by="from_leaders", size_by="size", label_by="label", width=320, height=360, legend=False, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {#349f01c8 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} karate.set_node_attrs("known", None) karate.set_node_attrs("known", {"16": 1, "26": 2}) guess = karate.harmonic_function(label_name="known") karate.set_node_attrs("from_16_26", guess) karate.set_node_attrs("size", 1) karate.set_node_attrs("size", 2, nodes=["16", "26"]) karate.plot( layout="pos", color_by="from_16_26", size_by="size", label_by="label", width=320, height=360, legend=False, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: ### Running to convergence `max_iter=` sets the number of propagation steps. From members 16 and 26, the default 30 is not enough to settle the scores, and with more steps the errors grow, until even the instructor is placed on the administrator's side: ::: {#4876b0a6 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} rows = [] for steps in (10, 30, 100, 300): guess = karate.harmonic_function(label_name="known", max_iter=steps) karate.set_node_attrs("guess", guess) members = karate.get_node_df() wrong = members.filter(pl.col("guess") != pl.col("faction")).height rows.append({"max_iter": steps, "wrong": wrong}) pl.DataFrame(rows) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
